references.text: In [ref:Luk 19:31|Luke 19:31], Jesus gives the disciples instructions on what to say if anyone asks: "The Lord has need of it." Verse 34 shows that the disciples obeyed and repeated exactly what Jesus had said.
In [ref:Mark 11:3-6|Mark 11:3-6], we find the parallel account where the disciples answer in the same way – "The Lord has need of it" – and the owners let them take the colt with them.

In [ref:Matt 21:3|Matthew 21:3], Jesus gives the same instruction to say that the Lord has need of the animals, which demonstrates Jesus' authority as Lord and his foreknowledge of how the situation would unfold.
[ref:Luk 19:33|Luke 19:33] describes how the owners actually asked the disciples why they were untying the colt, just as Jesus had predicted. Verse 34 is the direct answer to this question.

In [ref:Joh 13:13|John 13:13], Jesus says: "You call me Teacher and Lord, and you are right, for that is what I am." The title "Lord" (ὁ κύριος) used in Luke 19:34 confirms Jesus' lordship and authority.
[ref:1 Kor 10:26|1 Corinthians 10:26] quotes Psalm 24:1: "For the earth and everything in it belongs to the Lord." Jesus' claim on the colt reflects his sovereign rule over all creation.
